mastLead: Stranded capacity is not one failure. It is a family of them, spread across three layers — and each one is invisible to the metrics that watch the other two.
entryIsBody: A name, a boundary and a signal. What the phenomenon is, what it is not, and what you would have to observe to say it is present.
entryIsNotBody: A measurement. Nothing on this page is derived from data collected for this index. Naming has to come before counting.

def.lead: The industry reports how much capacity is installed and how much is utilized. Neither number describes the distance between them. This chapter defines that distance.
def.cardQuote: Stranded capacity is capacity that has been committed, is physically present, and cannot be used to serve demand that exists.
def.src: PhysaFlow Stranded Capacity Index · Definition v0.1 · open for comment
def.notLede: Six adjacent terms are already in use. None of them describes the same thing, and treating them as synonyms is how the gap stays invisible.

not.d: Capacity that is not in use right now.
not.b: Stranded capacity is always idle. Idle capacity is not always stranded — if no demand exists, the capacity is simply unused, and nothing is being lost.

not.d: A ratio between what is used and what is available.
not.b: A measurement, not a cause. Stranded capacity is one of several things that can produce a low ratio, and the ratio alone does not tell you which.

not.d: A deliberate decision to build beyond expected demand.
not.b: Intentional and planned for. Stranded capacity is the unintended residue that appears after the decision, often for reasons unrelated to it.

not.d: Capacity held on purpose for resilience or growth.
not.b: Working exactly as designed. Part of it still never produces output, so this index names it (FAC-05) instead of excluding it — but it is not a failure.

not.d: In finance and energy: assets written down early due to market or regulatory change.
not.b: A different field and a different mechanism. This index borrows the adjective because it is precise, not the underlying model.

not.d: In power systems: deliberately reducing available generation.
not.b: Supply-side and voluntary. Stranded capacity is involuntary and sits on the demand-facing side of the meter.

def.whyLede: Naming is not a formality. It is the precondition for everything that follows.

why.title: You cannot measure what you cannot name
why.body: There is no field in any standard reporting format for the capacity described above. It is absorbed into utilization, where it becomes indistinguishable from low demand.

why.title: You cannot compare across facilities
why.body: Two sites reporting the same utilization can have entirely different amounts of capacity they cannot reach. Without a shared name, the comparison is not possible.

why.title: You cannot price it
why.body: Capacity that cannot be named cannot be written into a contract, a service level or a valuation. It stays a private operational problem instead of a market one.

def.whereLede: The definition holds across three layers. Eighteen named phenomena satisfy all three conditions — seven in the facility, six in IT, five in workload and operations.

where.name: Facility
where.body: Electrical, thermal and spatial limits of the building itself.

where.name: IT
where.body: Hardware present in the building but not reachable as a usable set.

where.name: Workload and operations
where.body: Admission, placement and reservation behaviour once hardware is reachable.

stmtStrip.d: Capital has already been spent. A plan is not stranded capacity.
Physically in a building, identifiable. A forecast is not.
Demand exists that it cannot serve. That is the condition that separates it.

meth.lead: This index names phenomena it has not measured. Everything in this chapter exists to keep that distinction visible.
meth.statusQuote: No measurement has been collected for any entry or any figure in this index.
meth.src: PhysaFlow Stranded Capacity Index · Methodology v0.1 · open for comment
meth.qualifyLede: Five tests. The first three come from the definition. The last two are editorial, and exist so the taxonomy stays usable as it grows.

qualify.title: 01 · Committed
qualify.body: A plan or a budget line does not qualify. The money has to be out the door.

qualify.title: 02 · Present
qualify.def: Physically in a building and identifiable.
qualify.body: A forecast does not qualify. Someone has to be able to point at it.

qualify.title: 03 · Unreachable by demand
qualify.def: Demand exists that this capacity cannot serve.
qualify.body: This is the condition that separates stranded capacity from capacity that is merely unused.

qualify.title: 04 · Distinguishable
qualify.def: It can be told apart from the entries next to it.
qualify.body: If two entries always appear together and never apart, they are one entry with two names.

qualify.title: 05 · Falsifiable
qualify.def: At least one observable signal could confirm or deny it.
qualify.body: Without a signal, the entry cannot ever be tested — and an untestable entry has no place in an index.

meth.labelsLede: Six labels, two for names and four for figures. They exist so no reader has to guess how much weight a statement carries.

labels.title: Established term
labels.def: Used on names. Thirteen of eighteen entries.
labels.body: The name already exists in public literature. This index adopts it and defines its boundary more tightly.

labels.title: Proposed here
labels.def: Used on names. Five of eighteen entries.
labels.body: No agreed name was identified in public sources. This index proposes one, and it is open for comment.

labels.title: Illustrative model
labels.def: Used on figures. One figure carries it today.
labels.body: The shape is a hypothesis. Proportions carry no information and must not be read as quantities.

labels.title: Conceptual example
labels.def: Used on figures. Not in use yet.
labels.body: A worked case built to explain a mechanism. Not drawn from any real facility.

labels.title: Modelled
labels.def: Used on figures. Not in use yet.
labels.body: Derived from published inputs through a stated calculation. Nothing has reached this label.

labels.title: Measured
labels.def: Used on figures. Not in use yet.
labels.body: Built from telemetry collected under a published protocol. Nothing has reached this label.

meth.measureLabel: What would have to be measured
meth.measureLede: Each layer needs a different dataset, held by a different party, hard to obtain for a different reason.

measure.title: Facility
measure.def: Building management and DCIM records, plus utility interconnection filings.
measure.body: Operators and utilities. DCIM data is commercially sensitive, and interconnection queues are public in some jurisdictions and not in others.

measure.title: IT
measure.def: Scheduler inventory, node health state and fabric topology.
measure.body: Cluster operators. Rarely published, and the schema differs between schedulers, so comparing across sites needs a mapping that does not yet exist.

measure.title: Workload and operations
measure.def: Job accounting logs: requests, allocations, runtimes and exit states.
measure.body: The same operators. Publicly accessible supercomputing facilities are the only class that publishes this openly, which is why the index starts there.

meth.claimsLabel: What this index does not claim
meth.claimsLede: Stated up front, because an index of things nobody has counted is easy to misread — and easier to misquote.

claims.title: No global figure
claims.def: This index does not estimate how much capacity is stranded anywhere.
claims.body: No such number is published here. Any figure attributed to this index that does not appear on this site did not come from it.

claims.title: No judgement of any operator
claims.def: Naming a phenomenon is not an accusation.
claims.body: Most entries describe constraints that competent operators manage deliberately, and several describe systems working exactly as designed.

claims.title: No claim about relative size
claims.def: The eighteen entries are not ranked.
claims.body: Nothing here suggests fragmentation matters more than interconnection delay, or the reverse. The order is structural, not hierarchical.

claims.title: No claim of completeness
claims.def: Eighteen is what we could define and defend.
claims.body: The taxonomy is expected to grow, and entries are expected to merge or split as their boundaries get tested.

claims.title: No causal model
claims.def: The funnel shows seven steps in sequence, not a chain of causes.
claims.body: It does not claim that each step causes the next, or that removing one constraint releases capacity downstream.

claims.title: No institutional endorsement
claims.def: Institutions are cited or acknowledged, never claimed as reviewers.
claims.body: None of the institutions named anywhere on this site has reviewed, approved or endorsed this index.

meth.versioningLede: Every version is dated and kept. Nothing is edited silently.

versioning.title: What moves 0.1 to 0.2
versioning.body: Any entry added, removed or merged. Any change to a boundary. Any figure that moves from illustrative to modelled.

versioning.title: What moves 0.x to 1.0
versioning.body: At least one figure supported by measurement collected under a published protocol, and a taxonomy that has survived external review.

versioning.title: How to comment
versioning.body: Entries can be cited individually from the taxonomy. Disagreement about a boundary is the most useful comment this draft can receive.

refs.missingLede: Named openly, so nobody has to discover it by looking.

missing.title: Per-entry citations
missing.body: Each of the thirteen established terms should point to a document where the term is used, not only to a field. That work has not been done.

missing.title: A measurement protocol
missing.body: No source here describes how any of the eighteen phenomena would be measured. That protocol does not exist yet, in this index or elsewhere.

missing.title: Peer review

about.lead: Pioneers in the analysis of physical infrastructure for the generative AI era.
about.cardQuote: Untangling the most complex operational challenges facing modern data centers as the compute scale of AI models expands globally.
about.missionLede: Independent research for technology leaders, facility engineers and decision makers.
about.missionBody: Our reports and research provide analytical clarity to optimize performance and reduce infrastructure waste.
about.missionNote: Open data, replicable metrics and mandatory attribution of figures.
about.pillarsLede: Three principles back every report in the Stranded Capacity Index.

pillars.title: Replicable metrics
pillars.body: Every published figure can be recomputed from the source data.

pillars.title: Cited sources
pillars.body: No claim enters the index without a specific, dated source.

pillars.title: Open attribution
pillars.body: Figures are open material; citing them is mandatory and free.
